The problem is that I'm creating a new `UIViewController` for the `AdaptiveBottomSheet` and I'm passing `currentCompositionLocalContext` to the bottom sheet content, but this also overrides the new `UIViewController` with the old one, so the `AdaptiveDatePicker` gets drawn on the wrong view behind the bottom sheet.

This gets fixed or at least improved recently: https://github.com/JetBrains/compose-multiplatform/issues/4818

Customizing iOS native components is tricky, they don't give the same freedom as Compose. For now what I managed to do is: - `containerColor`: Will update the background color of the picker - ~`selectedDayContentColor`: Will update the tint color~ - `selectedDayContainerColor`: Will update the tint color - `dayContentColor`: Currently only white and black are supported (Handled by the component theme), when you choose a color, I will look if it's more white or black and then set the theme of the date picker which will change the text color accordingly. ```kotlin DatePickerDefaults.colors( selectedDayContainerColor = Color.Red, dayContentColor = Color.DarkGray, containerColor = Color.LightGray ) ``` This will be available in the next release and the [snapshot](https://mohamedrejeb.github.io/Calf/installation/#snapshots) version.

I will try `confirmValueChange`, what I tried is changing `skipPartiallyExpanded` and the sheet value was changed to `Hidden` and then changed back to `HalfExpanded` or `Expanded` depends on the value of `skipPartiallyExpanded`.
After this fix, the sheet value stays correct.
